segments.t: They say Cupid guides the fate of lovers with his bow, though sometimes he seems to have terrible eyesight and a strange sense of humor. The morning after Chef Barinov's birthday party, Denis happily brings Katya breakfast in bed—until Katya wakes up horrified and switches straight back into strict boss mode.
Купидон решает судьбы всех влюблённых людей.
Но иногда у него странное чувство юмора.
Доброе утро, соня, я приготовил завтрак!
Я уже успел сходить утром в душ.
Немедленно отвернись от меня, пожалуйста!
Ты такая смешная, когда крепко спишь.
Прекрати сейчас же всю эту нежную ерунду!
Но вчера вечером ты говорила совсем другое!
Вчера говорил напиток, а сейчас говорит начальник!
Через полчаса жду тебя на рабочем месте!
Если опоздаешь на работу, я тебя оштрафую!
Федя, вставай, наша новая начальница очень злая!
Let's step through the morning-after awakening between Denis and Katya.

'Cupid decides the fates of all people in love.' Notice how Russian puts 'cupid' and 'people' together in a short, direct phrase where word endings show how the ideas connect.

'But sometimes he has a strange sense of humor.' Russians say 'by me' or 'with us' where English says 'I have' or 'we have', without needing a separate word for 'have'.

'Good morning, sleepyhead, I made breakfast!' Denis uses a polite everyday Russian courtesy expression that sets the tone of the conversation right away.
Я уже успел сходить утром в душ.
'I already managed to take a shower in the morning.' Denis pairs 'already' with 'shower' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.

'Turn away from me immediately, please!' Katya uses a polite everyday Russian courtesy expression that sets the tone of the conversation right away.

'You are so funny when you are fast asleep.' Here Denis anchors the thought on 'funny, ridiculous' and finishes on 'sleep', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Прекрати сейчас же всю эту нежную ерунду!
'Stop all this mushy nonsense right now!' In everyday Russian, 'to stop, quit' flows straight into 'nonsense, trifle, nothing' without extra linking words.
Но вчера вечером ты говорила совсем другое!
'But last night you were saying something completely different!' Denis pairs 'yesterday' with 'other, different' directly, since spoken Russian skips English filler words like 'the', 'a', and 'is'.
Вчера говорил напиток, а сейчас говорит начальник!
'Yesterday the drink was speaking, and now the boss is speaking!' Katya contrasts past and present verbs to reassert her authority.
Через полчаса жду тебя на рабочем месте!
'In half an hour I expect you at your workstation!' Here Katya anchors the thought on 'half-hour' and finishes on 'place', keeping the spoken rhythm brisk and natural.
Если опоздаешь на работу, я тебя оштрафую!
'If you are late for work, I will fine you!' In everyday Russian, 'will be late' flows straight into 'will fine' without extra linking words.
